title: A Patch of Red

patient.name: Mr Wong Ah Kow
patient.presenting_complaint: Bright red patch on the white of one eye, no pain, vision normal

history.hpc: Mr Wong says 'This morning I see one big red patch on my eye, look very scary, but no pain and I can see okay.' One eye, a flat bright-red patch on the sclera, no pain, no discharge, no change in vision. No injury he can recall.
history.pmhx: High blood pressure. Takes aspirin daily.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Flat bright-red area over the sclera, cornea clear by observation, no discharge

investigations.history_and_triage: Focused history shows a painless red patch with normal vision and no discharge — typical of a subconjunctival haemorrhage, often benign, with relevant aspirin use and high blood pressure noted.
investigations.red_flags_checked: No pain, no visual loss, no discharge, no injury — no sight-threatening red flags.
investigations.triage_category: Routine — reassure; note the anticoagulant and blood pressure for the doctor; advise a blood pressure check.

diagnosis: A painless, flat, bright-red scleral patch with normal vision and no discharge is consistent with a subconjunctival haemorrhage, which is usually benign. The PSA reassures the patient, notes the aspirin and blood pressure as relevant, and routes routinely. No medical diagnosis is made by the PSA.

immediate: Confirm identity and take a focused red-eye history including injury and straining
Recognise the painless, normal-vision, no-discharge pattern of a subconjunctival haemorrhage
Ask about and note blood thinners (aspirin) and high blood pressure
Record visual acuity and triage routinely
follow_up: Suggest a blood pressure check and note the aspirin use for the doctor
Advise return if pain, vision change or recurrence
patient_education: Reassure that it usually looks worse than it is and clears over 1–2 weeks
Advise not to rub the eye
Advise reviewing blood pressure and returning if it recurs often
